results.title: The impact of ESG performance on OFDI mode choice - Nature
results.content: We construct a theoretical model of ESG performance affecting enterprises’ Outward Foreign Direct Investment (OFDI) mode choice from the perspective of total factor productivity and empirically tests the model using data from Chinese listed companies. Therefore, an in-depth exploration of how ESG influences corporate OFDI mode selection, and examining the mechanisms through which ESG performance affects OFDI mode choice from a productivity perspective, will not only help companies from various countries select the appropriate mode for international expansion while enhancing their internal ESG capabilities but also integrate ESG as new competitive advantage into classical international investment theory, thereby further expanding and enriching the theory of corporate international investment. Therefore, when enterprises choose the cross-border MandA mode and invest in sensitive industries (e.g., energy, scarce natural resources, and critical infrastructure), they tend to trigger vigilance from the host country government and may face direct or indirect obstruction, resulting in differences in how improving ESG performance influences the choice of OFDI mode.

results.title: ESG Performance and Total Factor Productivity - Evidence from China
results.content: While most of the studies provide evidence that the ESG significantly improves a firm's performance and value in the long run, few studies quantitatively analyzed the linkage between ESG and total factor productivity (TFP). A firm's ESG strategy initially enhances its ability to pursue innovative activities and then ultimately and positively impacts its financial/operational performance (Broadstock et al., 2021), thus improving the TFP of enterprises (Chang and Tang, 2021). Second, firms with a high-quality ESG performance are more effective in mitigating financial constraints and increasing TFP. Heavy pollution enterprises have to first strengthen the disclosure of ESG information so as to alleviate financial constraints (Luo, 2022), promote technological innovation (Broadstock et al., 2021), and thus have a positive impact on TFP.
